title: Teams and Microsoft 365 admin centers: unified management of Teams apps and agents across Teams, Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app
summary: The briefing's rollout phases, administrative paths, commands and licensing prerequisites are supported by the supplied records and Microsoft documentation. A minor checklist mismatch remains: the setup-policy installation inventory has no corresponding controls-table row.

claims.claim: The roadmap products are Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 Admin Center.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams", "Microsoft 365 Admin Center"]

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Desktop.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop"]

claims.claim: The roadmap target is July CY2024.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "July CY2024"

claims.claim: The roadmap record supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap says Integrated Apps changes previously affected these apps only on Outlook and the Microsoft 365 App.
claims.quote: Before this update, changes made through the Integrated Apps section in the Microsoft 365 admin center would only affect these apps on Outlook and the Microsoft 365 App

claims.claim: The roadmap says Teams admin center changes previously affected only Teams.
claims.quote: similarly, changes made in the Teams admin center would exclusively affect Teams.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Unified management lets administrators manage the cross-host apps and agents from either admin center across Teams, Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app.
claims.quote: With unified agent app management, you can now manage agents and apps via the Teams admin center or Integrated apps page in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Any changes made in either admin center are automatically synchronized.

claims.claim: Developers can enhance Teams apps to work in Outlook and the Microsoft 365 App.
claims.quote: App developers can enhance their Microsoft Teams apps to work in Outlook and in Microsoft 365 App (formerly known as Office.com).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After unification, org-wide setting changes synchronize between the admin centers.
claims.quote: After unification, changes made to the app status, org-wide settings, and user assignment in either admin center are synchronized in the other.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: After unification, app status changes synchronize between the admin centers.
claims.quote: After unification, changes made to the app status, org-wide settings, and user assignment in either admin center are synchronized in the other.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[4].note
claims.claim: After unification, app availability and user assignments synchronize between the admin centers.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The default state is on because tenants that never modified either center's defaults, availability or block settings unify automatically.
claims.quote: If your tenant never modified its org-wide defaults, app availability, or app block or unblock settings in either TAC or MAC, then your tenant's app availability policies are automatically unified.

claims.claim: Modified tenants can choose to unify using Move to unified app management.
claims.quote: Select Move to unified app management. A dialog box appears to ask for your consent to move to the unified agent and app management experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Where settings differ, the wizard lets an administrator choose which admin center's settings to apply.
claims.quote: Select the admin center’s settings that you want to apply from the Apply settings from drop-down list and select Apply settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Only a Global admin can give final consent and apply unification changes.
claims.quote: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final changes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Roles
claims.claim: A Teams or Global admin can prepare updates through Review summary.
claims.quote: Any Teams or Global admin can make updates upto the Review summary page.

claims.claim: MC796790 contains a text update dated 18 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 18, 2026: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available.

claims.claim: Phase 1 rollout for never-modified tenants began in late September 2025.
claims.quote: App and agent availability unification (Section A): Rollout began in late September 2025.

claims.claim: Phase 2 for modified tenants is described as fully rolled out.
claims.quote: This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Phase 2 applies no org-wide or app-level setting changes without administrator action.
claims.quote: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Future Phase 3 will automatically unify tenants that have not acted.
claims.quote: Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft promises the Phase 3 timeline at least 60 days before it begins.
claims.quote: We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not yet announced a Phase 3 start date in the supplied notice.
claims.quote: The Phase 3 timeline will be announced separately, at least 60 days before that phase begins.

claims.claim: The notice says unified app and agent installation management is generally available.
claims.quote: Updated November 18, 2026: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available.

claims.claim: Installation unification applies to tenants whose availability has been unified.
claims.quote: Tenants whose app and agent availability has been unified through any of the phases described in section A are eligible.

claims.claim: Supported app and agent installations synchronize across the centers within 24 to 48 hours after availability unification.
claims.quote: For any tenant that unifies app/agent availability through Phase 1, Phase 2, or Phase 3, app and agent installations are also unified across the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) and Teams admin center (TAC) within 24–48 hours of completing availability unification.

claims.claim: The notice says app installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies.
claims.quote: Important: App installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Installations previously made through Teams app setup policies are not unified by this change.
claims.quote: Installations previously made through those policies are not unified as part of this change.

claims.claim: MC796790 associates roadmap items 393931, 485712 and 503105.
claims.quote: This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

claims.where: Why it matters: first paragraph; What's changing: comparison of guides
claims.claim: Before unification, settings must be maintained in both centers, and Microsoft advises keeping them synchronized to prevent disruption.
claims.quote: Until your tenant is migrated to unified app management, ensure that the settings in both admin centers, such as blocked apps or org-wide app settings, remain synchronized. This measure prevents unexpected disruptions or issues with agent and app functionality.

claims.claim: Microsoft's feature documentation describes no new data access introduced by the unification step.
claims.quote: Searched: '"unified app management" "data access"'; read uam-tac-mac, manage-apps and supplied MC796790. They describe availability, status, org-wide settings and installation synchronization, not new data permissions.

claims.claim: After unification synchronization is automatic in both directions rather than requiring approval of each change.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.claim: Microsoft names Teams Administrator as the role for using Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.claim: A Teams administrator's post-unification app status or availability changes influence Outlook and Microsoft 365 app availability.
claims.quote: Ensures org-wide defaults for both admin centers are in sync and governs app availability across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft Copilot apps

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Availability changes take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: In rare cases availability changes take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Agent management requires the organization's required subscription and licenses for Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot or Microsoft Agent 365.
claims.quote: Your organization has the required subscription and licenses for either Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, or Microsoft Agent 365.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Users who create, publish or use agents must have appropriate licenses assigned.
claims.quote: Users at your organization that create, publish, or use agents have the appropriate licenses assigned.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included in the applicable underlying Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot or Microsoft Agent 365 licensing.
claims.quote: The following licensing options include agents that can be managed in Microsoft 365 admin center:

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate license for the unification step itself is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'unified agent app management license requirements included Microsoft 365', '"unified app management" "licensing"'. Read uam-tac-mac and agent-365-overview prerequisites and licensing; no separate unification license is specified.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate consumption meter for unification itself is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'unified app management unification PowerShell API tenant migration status licence pricing meter', '"unified agent and app management" "cost"'. Read uam-tac-mac and agent-365-overview; neither specifies a meter for synchronizing admin settings.

claims.claim: Individual third-party apps can have their own publisher-provided paid subscriptions or licenses.
claims.quote: Some Teams apps require purchasing a service subscription to use app functionality. These service subscriptions are called Software as a Service (SaaS) offers.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, export catalogue
claims.claim: Administrators can export the app catalogue from Teams admin center to review status and availability.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can export the entire agent and app catalog for your org from the Teams admin center. It can help you to coordinate with admin and security teams to evaluate agents and apps, verify availability, verify status, and more.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center route to tenant unification is Teams apps > Manage apps > Move to unified app management.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. The Manage apps page appears. ... Select Move to unified app management. The Align org-wide app settings page appears.

claims.claim: No PowerShell or API operation for the tenant unification step is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"unified app management" "PowerShell"', '"unified app management" "API" "migration"'. Read uam-tac-mac and Update-M365TeamsApp; the former gives the consent wizard, the latter changes app settings, not tenant migration.

claims.claim: Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block controls an individual app or agent's allowed or blocked status.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams module's Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -IsBlocked $true sets an app's state.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

claims.claim: The printed Teams route through an app's Users and groups tab, Availability selector and Edit availability reaches app access management.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. ... Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. ... Select Edit availability.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app ID> -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups -OperationType Add -Groups <group IDs> adds group availability assignments.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.

claims.claim: Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Custom apps > Let users install and use available apps by default reaches the Custom apps switch.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. ... Under Custom apps, turn off or turn on Let users install and use available apps by default option.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp -isSideloadedAppsInteractionEnabled $True sets the Custom Apps switch in the MicrosoftTeams module.
claims.quote: There is a switch for managing Custom Apps in the Org-wide App Settings page of Teams Admin Center. The command can set the value of this switch. If the isSideloadedAppsInteractionEnabled is set to true, the switch is enabled.

claims.claim: Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Users > Specific users/group in the organization can install sets selective self-install availability in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Select Settings, then select Integrated Apps. ... Select the Available Apps list. ... select the app you want to edit. ... select the Users tab in the overview pane. ... Specific users/group in the organization can install

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center side has no documented automation operation for its cross-host self-install availability control.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Integrated apps cross application availability users groups PowerShell Graph API', '"Integrated apps" "availability" "API"'. Read cross-application guide and Update-M365TeamsApp; no MAC-side operation is specified.

claims.claim: App availability cannot be updated in bulk in Teams admin center but can be through PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell.

claims.claim: The unification wizard includes Align org-wide app settings, Align app-level settings, bulk app resolution and Review summary.
claims.quote: Bulk app resolution: Select multiple apps at a time and select either Teams admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center from the Apply settings from drop-down list. Use this setting to apply changes in bulk across all apps from either one of the admin centers.

claims.claim: The cited cross-application app guide limits its Integrated apps controls to Global Admins.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins. Check your credentials before you proceed.

claims.claim: The cross-application guide does not explain how its Global Admin restriction interacts with the Teams Administrator role after unification.
claims.quote: Searched: '"unified agent and app management" "Global" "role"'. Read cross-application guide and uam-tac-mac; the former limits its controls to Global Admins, while the latter describes wizard roles and synchronization without resolving that interaction.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The documented work is administrative alignment, with no separate unification charge stated in the reviewed sources.
claims.quote: Searched: '"unified app" "pricing"', '"unified agent and app management" "cost"'. Read uam-tac-mac and agent-365-overview: alignment steps and underlying licenses are documented, but no unification price or meter is specified.

claims.claim: The Custom Apps cmdlet controls that switch, not the Microsoft apps or Third-party apps switches.
claims.quote: Set the Custom Apps Setting's value of Teams Admin Center.

claims.claim: The cmdlet documentation does not explain how each call appears in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Update-M365TeamsApp" "Microsoft 365 admin center"'. Read Update-M365TeamsApp and Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp references; they describe Teams settings and do not specify each call's MAC presentation.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, setup-policy installation inventory
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks the reader to take stock of is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'List apps that users received through Teams app setup policies'. The table covers tenant unification, app blocking, app availability, Custom apps and MAC availability, but not setup-policy installation assignments.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'List apps that users received through Teams app setup policies'. Keep the supported setup-policy installation limitation in Risk assessment.
